In this situation, the best option is to use\\n189/// [`Bencher::iter`] which has next-to-zero measurement overhead.\\n190#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq, Copy, Hash, Clone)]\\n191pub enum BatchSize {\\n192    /// `SmallInput` indicates that the input to the benchmark routine (the value returned from\\n193    /// the setup routine) is small enough that millions of values can be safely held in memory.\\n194    /// Always prefer `SmallInput` unless the benchmark is using too much memory.\\n195    ///\\n196    /// In testing, the maximum measurement overhead from benchmarking with `SmallInput` is on the\\n197    /// order of 500 picoseconds. This is presented as a rough guide; your results may vary.\\n198    SmallInput,\\n199\\n200    /// `LargeInput` indicates that the input to the benchmark routine or the value returned from\\n201    /// that routine is large. This will reduce the memory usage but increase the measurement\\n202    /// overhead.\\n203    ///\\n204    /// In testing, the maximum measurement overhead from benchmarking with `LargeInput` is on the\\n205    /// order of 750 picoseconds. This is presented as a rough guide; your results may vary.\\n206    LargeInput,\\n207\\n208    /// `PerIteration` indicates that the input to the benchmark routine or the value returned from\\n209    /// that routine is extremely large or holds some limited resource, such that holding many values\\n210    /// in memory at once is infeasible. This provides the worst measurement overhead, but the\\n211    /// lowest memory usage.\\n212    ///\\n213    /// In testing, the maximum measurement overhead from benchmarking with `PerIteration` is on the\\n214    /// order of 350 nanoseconds or 350,000 picoseconds. This is presented as a rough guide; your\\n215    /// results may vary.\\n216    PerIteration,\\n217\\n218    /// `NumBatches` will attempt to divide the iterations up into a given number of batches.\\n219    /// A larger number of batches (and thus smaller batches) will reduce memory usage but increase\\n220    /// measurement overhead. This allows the user to choose their own tradeoff between memory usage\\n221    /// and measurement overhead, but care must be taken in tuning the number of batches. Most\\n222    /// benchmarks should use `SmallInput` or `LargeInput` instead.\\n223    NumBatches(u64),\\n224\\n225    /// `NumIterations` fixes the batch size to a constant number, specified by the user. This\\n226    /// allows the user to choose their own tradeoff between overhead and memory usage, but care must\\n227    /// be taken in tuning the batch size. In general, the measurement overhead of `NumIterations`\\n228    /// will be larger than that of `NumBatches`. Most benchmarks should use `SmallInput` or\\n229    /// `LargeInput` instead.\\n230    NumIterations(u64),\\n231\\n232    #[doc(hidden)]\\n233    __NonExhaustive,\\n234}\\n235impl BatchSize {\\n236    /// Convert to a number of iterations per batch.\\n237    ///\\n238    /// We try to do a constant number of batches regardless of the number of iterations in this\\n239    /// sample. If the measurement overhead is roughly constant regardless of the number of\\n240    /// iterations the analysis of the results later will have an easier time separating the\\n241    /// measurement overhead from the benchmark time.\\n242    fn iters_per_batch(self, iters: u64) -> u64 {\\n243        match self {\\n244            BatchSize::SmallInput => (iters + 10 - 1) / 10,\\n245            BatchSize::LargeInput => (iters + 1000 - 1) / 1000,\\n246            BatchSize::PerIteration => 1,\\n247            BatchSize::NumBatches(batches) => (iters + batches - 1) / batches,\\n248            BatchSize::NumIterations(size) => size,\\n249            BatchSize::__NonExhaustive => panic!(\\\"__NonExhaustive is not a valid BatchSize.\\\"),\\n250        }\\n251    }\\n252}\\n253\\n254/// Baseline describes how the `baseline_directory` is handled.\\n255#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\\n256pub enum Baseline {\\n257    /// `CompareLenient` compares against a previous saved version of the baseline.\\n258    /// If a previous baseline does not exist, the benchmark is run as normal but no comparison occurs.\\n259    CompareLenient,\\n260    /// `CompareStrict` compares against a previous saved version of the baseline.\\n261    /// If a previous baseline does not exist, a panic occurs.\\n262    CompareStrict,\\n263    /// `Save` writes the benchmark results to the baseline directory,\\n264    /// overwriting any results that were previously there.\\n265    Save,\\n266    /// `Discard` benchmark results.\\n267    Discard,\\n268}\\n269\\n270/// Enum used to select the plotting backend.\\n271///\\n272/// See [`Criterion::plotting_backend`].\\n273#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]\\n274pub enum PlottingBackend {\\n275    /// Plotting backend which uses the external `gnuplot` command to render plots. This is the\\n276    /// default if the `gnuplot` command is installed.\\n277    Gnuplot,\\n278    /// Plotting backend which uses the Rust 'Plotters' library. This is the default if `gnuplot`\\n279    /// is not installed.\\n280    Plotters,\\n281    /// Null plotting backend which outputs nothing,\\n282    None,\\n283}\\n284impl PlottingBackend {\\n285    fn create_plotter(&self) -> Option<Box<dyn Plotter>> {\\n286        match self {\\n287            PlottingBackend::Gnuplot => Some(Box::<Gnuplot>::default()),\\n288            #[cfg(feature = \\\"plotters\\\")]\\n289            PlottingBackend::Plotters => Some(Box::<PlottersBackend>::default()),\\n290            #[cfg(not(feature = \\\"plotters\\\"))]\\n291            PlottingBackend::Plotters => panic!(\\\"Criterion was built without plotters support.\\\"),\\n292            PlottingBackend::None => None,\\n293        }\\n294    }\\n295}\\n296\\n297#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\\n298/// Enum representing the execution mode.\\n299pub(crate) enum Mode {\\n300    /// Run benchmarks normally.\\n301    Benchmark,\\n302    /// List all benchmarks but do not run them.\\n303    List(ListFormat),\\n304    /// Run benchmarks once to verify that they work, but otherwise do not measure them.\\n305    Test,\\n306    /// Iterate benchmarks for a given length of time but do not and \\\": benchmark\\\" at the end\\n326    /// is printed out.\\n327    Terse,\\n328}\\n329\\n330/// Benchmark filtering support.\\n331#[derive(Clone, Debug)]\\n332pub enum BenchmarkFilter {\\n333   /// Creates a benchmark manager with the following default settings:\\n395    ///\\n396    /// - Sample size: 100 measurements\\n397    /// - Warm-up time: 3 s\\n398    /// - Measurement time: 5 The noise threshold\\n580    /// is used to filter out small changes in performance, even if they are statistically\\n581    /// significant. Sometimes benchmarking the same code twice will result in small but\\n582    /// statistically significant differences solely because of noise. This provides a way to filter\\n583    /// out some of these false positives at the cost of making it harder to detect small changes\\n584    /// to the true performance of the benchmark.\\n585    ///\\n586    /// The default is 0.01, meaning that changes smaller than 1% will be ignored.\\n587    ///\\n588    /// # Panics\\n589    ///\\n590    /// Panics if the threshold is set to a negative value\\n591    pub fn noise_threshold(mut self, threshold: f64) -> Criterion<M> {\\n592        assert!(threshold >= 0.0);\\n593\\n594        self.config.noise_threshold = threshold;\\n595        self\\n596    }\\n597\\n598    #[must_use]\\n599    /// Changes the default confidence level for benchmarks run with this runner. The default is\\n602    /// 0.95, meaning that the confidence interval should capture the true value 95% of the time.\\n603    ///\\n604    /// # Panics\\n605    ///\\n606    /// Panics if the confidence level is set to a value outside the `(0, 1)` range\\n607    pub fn confidence_level(mut self, cl: f64) -> Criterion<M> {\\n608        assert!(cl > 0.0 && cl < 1.0);\\n609        if cl < 0.5 {\\n610            eprintln!(\\\"\\\\nWarning: It is not recommended to reduce confidence level below 0.5.\\\");\\n611        }\\n612\\n613        self.config.confidence_level = cl;\\n614        self\\n615    }\\n616\\n617    #[must_use]\\n618    /// Changes the default [significance level](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistical_significance)\\n619    /// for benchmarks run with this runner. This is used to perform a\\n620    /// [hypothesis test](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Statistical_hypothesis_testing) to see if\\n621    /// the measurements from this run are different from the measured performance of the last run.\\n622    /// The significance level is the desired probability that two measurements of identical code\\n623    /// will be considered 'different' due to noise in the measurements.
